Both identity pools should be attached to their respective roles, and the template should output the identity pool IDs, user pool IDs, and client IDs for both setups.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a scheduled workflow to automatically close AWS Organization accounts that are tagged with the key "organizations:account-closure" and value "REQUESTED". The workflow should run every hour via an EventBridge rule, invoking an EXPRESS Step Functions state machine that paginates through accounts tagged for closure, describes each account, and if it is ACTIVE, closes it using the Organizations CloseAccount API, then tags the account with "ACKNOWLEDGED". The state machine must include error handling for throttling and eventual consistency, log all execution data to a CloudWatch log group with a 365-day retention, and use IAM roles with least-privilege permissions scoped to the required Organizations and tagging actions.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the shared IAM roles and instance profiles required by the Amazon EKS Quick Start stacks in our account, using the prefix "eks-quickstart" for all role names and storing parameter values under the SSM path "/quickstart/amazon-eks". The template should provision Lambda execution roles for various EKS operations including copying zip artifacts from S3, reading resource information (with read-only access across the account in addition to basic Lambda execution permissions), creating the VPC role, deleting bucket contents, cleaning up load balancers, cleaning up security group dependencies, cleaning up Lambda functions, resolving caller ARNs, registering custom resource types, managing node security groups, creating Fargate profiles, and resolving SSM parameters, along with the EKS control plane role that can be assumed by the EKS service, attaches the AWS managed AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSServicePolicy policies, and additionally allows describing EC2 account attributes, addresses, and internet gateways; the Fargate execution role that can be assumed by the EKS Fargate pods service; and both managed and unmanaged node instance roles with corresponding instance profiles that can be assumed by EC2 instances, attach the AWS managed AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, and AmazonElasticFileSystemReadOnlyAccess policies, and also allow signaling stack completion back to CloudFormation; plus the role creation role that allows Lambda to create the fixed-name IAM role "CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC" and to attach only the AWS managed AWSLambdaENIManagementAccess and AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole policies to that specific role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS AppSync GraphQL API named "WS-API" with API_KEY authentication, designed to support real-time WebSocket communication through subscriptions and mutations. The API must include a schema defining a "Channel" type with "name" (String!) and "data" (AWSJSON!) fields, along with Query, Mutation, and Subscription types: a "getChannel" query, a "publish2channel" mutation that accepts "name" (String!) and "data" (AWSJSON!) and returns a Channel, and a "subscribe2channel" subscription that accepts a "name" (String!) and is annotated to trigger on the "publish2channel" mutation. The API should use a NONE-type data source named "pubsub" for the resolver, and the resolver for the publish2channel mutation must be a UNIT resolver that passes the arguments directly as the payload. The template should also create a default API key and expose the GraphQL URL, API key, API ID, and region as outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito User Pool for an AgentOps e-commerce analytics demo, with a public app client configured for SRP and refresh token authentication, three user groups (team-alpha with precedence 10, team-beta with precedence 20, and admin with precedence 1), and a custom resource Lambda function that seeds six test users, all sharing the same demo password value hardcoded in the seeding logic (for example, Demo1234!) so the template is fully self-contained: alice@demo.local and bob@demo.local in team-alpha with a custom role attribute of member, charlie@demo.local in team-alpha with a custom role attribute of team_admin, dave@demo.local in team-beta with a custom role attribute of member, eve@demo.local in team-beta with a custom role attribute of team_admin, and admin@demo.local in the admin group with a custom role attribute of admin. The user pool should be named agentops-ecommerce-users, the app client agentops-web-client, and the OAuth callback URL set to http://localhost:3000/auth/callback for local development. The template must also include appropriate outputs for the user pool ID, ARN, client ID, region, and seeder function ARN, with the user pool supporting email verification, optional MFA via software tokens, and a password policy requiring at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and numbers.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route53 hosted zone for a parameterized domain (defaulting to earhustlesq.com) and configures the full set of DNS records required for the production environment of the Ear Hustle application, including TXT records for SPF, Google site verification, Zoom verification, DMARC, and ATProto; MX records for G Suite email on both the primary domain and an old subdomain; A records pointing to Squarespace IPs and CNAMEs for www, podcast feeds, and Squarespace domain verification; ZenDesk TXT and CNAME records for verification, domain validation, and DKIM; Campaign Monitor DKIM, SPF alignment, and MX records; Google Workspace DKIM; Supercast DKIM and return-path CNAME; and an ACM certificate validation CNAME for the feeds subdomain using dynamically generated validation names and targets, with the hosted zone tagged with standard PRX tags including prx:ops:environment set to Production and prx:dev:application set to Ear Hustle.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain passengerlist.org, and provisions all necessary DNS record sets including TXT records for SPF and site verification, MX records for G Suite email with standard priority values, a DMARC TXT record on the _dmarc subdomain, A and AAAA alias records pointing the root domain and multiple subdomains (www, departures, join, athena, feed) to their respective CloudFront distributions using the standard CloudFront alias hosted zone ID, CNAME records for Zendesk mail routing, DKIM verification, and Squarespace domain verification, and CNAME records for AWS ACM certificate validation across several subdomains, using dynamically fetched or referenced values where those resources would be provisioned separately.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates IAM roles and managed policies for an e-commerce serverless architecture, including a role for a Lambda function that reads from an SQS queue named `POC-Queue-{env}` and writes to a DynamoDB table named `ecommerce-orders-{env}`, a second role for a Lambda function that reads from DynamoDB Streams on that same table and publishes to an SNS topic named `POC-Topic-{env}`, and a third role for API Gateway to send messages to the SQS queue, along with the necessary managed policies for these actions and a basic Lambda execution policy for CloudWatch logs, all parameterized by an Environment parameter with a default of `dev` and allowed values `dev`, `test`, `prod`, and with the role ARNs exported for cross-stack references.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 hosted zone for 'theworld.org' and populates it with a comprehensive set of DNS records to support a production media environment. The template must accept the domain name as a parameter (defaulting to 'theworld.org.') and apply standard organizational tags for the production environment. Configure a robust email security posture by creating a root TXT record combining SPF includes for Outlook, CreateSend, Google, Zendesk, and Sendergen, along with a DMARC record configured to reject failures and send reports to specified email addresses. Create MX records routing mail appropriately for the root domain, 'gsuite', 'o365', and 'bounce' subdomains. For web traffic, provision A and AAAA Alias records pointing to CloudFront distributions for various content subdomains (e.g., admin, api, projects, sitemap, feeds), and route the primary WordPress production and staging subdomains to their respective Application Load Balancers. Finally, include CNAME records for public feeds, Autodiscover endpoints, Zendesk mail routing, and AWS ACM validation records for the various subdomains, utilizing dummy values or parameters where appropriate for external endpoints and validation hashes.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC infrastructure for OpenSearch cross-region resilience, deployable in both regions, with a configurable environment name (default "production"), a VPC CIDR of 10.0.0.0/16, three private subnets (10.0.1.0/24, 10.0.2.0/24, 10.0.3.0/24) and three public subnets (10.0.101.0/24, 10.0.102.0/24, 10.0.103.0/24) each in separate Availability Zones, an Internet Gateway, and an optional NAT Gateway setup that can be either a single NAT Gateway (cost-effective) or one per AZ for high availability, with the default being single; the template should also enable VPC Flow Logs with a 7-day retention period sent to CloudWatch Logs, and export all subnet IDs, VPC ID, and NAT Gateway IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the required IAM roles for SageMaker project templates, allowing each role's creation to be controlled independently via a parameter that defaults to "YES" except for the launch role and use role which default to "NO", and each role should be scoped to the /service-role/ path with a maximum session duration of one hour, with the launch role and use role having a deletion policy of Retain, and the template must output all eleven role ARNs, including the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsExecutionRole attached to the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess managed policy, the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsLaunchRole attached to the AmazonSageMakerAdmin-ServiceCatalogProductsServiceRolePolicy, the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsUseRole attached to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy plus an inline policy granting specific permissions across SageMaker, CloudFormation, CloudWatch, CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CodePipeline, EC2 (including network interface management for VPC-connected jobs), ECR, Events, Firehose, Glue, IAM, Lambda, Logs, S3, Step Functions, CodeStar Connections, KMS, and SSM, and the remaining service roles for CloudFormation, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, Events, API Gateway, Firehose, Glue, and Lambda each having their respective AWS-managed service role policies attached.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-service Cognito user pool for testing JWT authentication flows with an AgentCore Gateway and MCP server, where users can sign up using their email address and verify themselves without any admin intervention by enabling self-service signup with email verification, and the pool should include a hosted UI domain for signup and login pages, a resource server with identifier "api" and custom scopes named "mcp" and "gateway", a public web client that supports authorization code with PKCE along with explicit auth flows for USER_PASSWORD_AUTH and USER_SRP_AUTH for programmatic testing with token validity set to 60 minutes for access and ID tokens and 30 days for refresh tokens, and two separate machine-to-machine clients that use the client credentials grant with the appropriate custom scopes for gateway and MCP server authentication, each with a generated client secret and token validity of 60 minutes for access and ID tokens and 1 day for refresh tokens, and the template should accept comma-delimited parameters for callback and logout URLs with sensible localhost defaults.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained Kinesis Firehose delivery stream configured for DirectPut delivery, which compresses incoming data using GZIP and buffers it for up to 900 seconds or 128 MB before writing to a newly provisioned S3 bucket under a "raw/MyKinesisFirehose/" prefix; the stack must also create that S3 bucket, a dedicated CloudWatch log group with a 14-day retention policy and a log stream named "firehose" to capture delivery stream logs, an IAM role that allows the Firehose service to assume it and grants permissions for S3 PutObject, GetObject, AbortMultipartUpload, GetBucketLocation, ListBucket, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on the target bucket and its prefix path as well as full CloudWatch Logs access on the created log group, and a CloudWatch alarm that monitors the DeliveryToS3.DataFreshness metric every 60 seconds with a threshold of 1800 seconds and treats missing data as not breaching.

We need a CloudFormation template that deploys an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway infrastructure for MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration to support an AI agent for protein variant effect prediction. The template should not provision the backend compute or authentication providers; instead, it must dynamically resolve existing configuration from SSM Parameter Store. Create an IAM role for the 'bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com' service that grants permission to invoke a Lambda function (retrieving the Lambda ARN dynamically from SSM) and store this new IAM role's ARN in a standard SSM parameter. Provision the AgentCore Gateway configured with a custom JWT authorizer that dynamically references a Cognito discovery URL and client ID from SSM. Next, create a gateway target connecting the gateway to the Lambda function, defining an MCP inline tool schema with 'invoke_endpoint' and 'get_results' operations for submitting sequences and checking job completion. Include parameters for the project name (defaulting to 'protein-engineering'), gateway description, and an optional gateway name that auto-generates from the project name if left blank.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS App Runner service for a multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard application, provisioning a new ECR repository and container image within the same account and region, with auto-deployments enabled and a health check at the /status path on port 8080, while also creating IAM roles: a build role with permissions to access ECR (including GetAuthorizationToken and image pull operations) and a task role with permissions to call Directory Service and QuickSight APIs (such as CreateNamespace, CreateDataSet, RegisterUser, and related actions) to support tenant provisioning, and configuring the App Runner service with runtime environment variables including ALLOW_IP_RANGE set to 0.0.0.0/0, the AWS region and account ID, a dummy email placeholder, an admin user name, and template, dataset, datasource, database, table, and filter column identifiers for the QuickSight integration, with the template being fully self-contained and outputting the generated image URI and the App Runner service URL.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a regional Web Application Firewall (WAFv2) for an Application Load Balancer. The stack must use a customizable prefix parameter (defaulting to 'sera', 3-21 lowercase characters) to name resources, and must accept two additional parameters for external dependencies: the ARN of an existing Application Load Balancer and the ARN of an existing KMS key. The WAF should allow traffic by default and include two rate limit rules: one blocking IPs exceeding 2000 requests per 5 minutes, and a stricter one blocking IPs exceeding 1000 requests per 5 minutes for URI paths containing '/api/'. Additionally, enable the AWS managed rule groups for common threats, known bad inputs, SQL injection, Linux operating system protection, and IP reputation. Associate the WAF with the provided ALB parameter, and configure CloudWatch logging (with 10-year retention, encrypted using the provided KMS key parameter), ensuring a logging filter is applied to only keep entries where the action was COUNT.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS Cognito authentication infrastructure for an application called "nih-grants", including a user pool with multi-factor authentication enabled and advanced security mode enforced, an identity pool that supports both authenticated and unauthenticated identities (with unauthenticated access disabled by default), and two app clients (one for web and one for general use) with a 30-day refresh token validity. The user pool must enforce a password policy requiring a minimum length of 11 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, with temporary passwords valid for 7 days, and email verification should use a confirmation code with the subject "Your verification code" and message "Your verification code is {####}". The authenticated IAM role should include an inline policy granting S3 object-level permissions (put, get, delete, and tagging) on a bucket named with the pattern "nih-grants-context-{region}-{accountId}", KMS GenerateDataKey and Decrypt permissions restricted to requests using the alias "nih-grants-s3-key", and API Gateway WebSocket connect permission on any API in the account and region. The identity pool must be linked to both app clients and the authenticated and unauthenticated roles should be attached via a role mapping.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Backup infrastructure to automatically back up all resources tagged with the key "backup" and values "daily", "weekly", and "monthly", with daily backups running each day at 5 AM UTC and retaining for 14 days, weekly backups each Sunday at 5 AM UTC retaining for 56 days, and monthly backups on the first day of each month at 5 AM UTC retaining for 365 days; the template should include separate encrypted backup vaults for each schedule, a KMS key with rotation enabled, an IAM service role for AWS Backup, and tag-based backup selections that use the specified tags, as well as provision Service Catalog TagOption key-value pairs for the backup tag values to integrate with Service Catalog portfolios and products, and all resources must be self-contained within the stack.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a SageMaker notebook instance for RAPIDS AI development, including an IAM role with the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess managed policy, a lifecycle configuration that installs a RAPIDS AI conda environment and registers a Jupyter kernel on notebook creation and start, and a GPU-enabled notebook instance of type ml.p3.2xlarge with 50 GB of storage, named "rapidsai", and configured to clone the default repository from https://github.com/rapidsai/notebooks.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates its own EKS cluster, two private subnets in the first two available availability zones, and the required security groups (an EMR cluster security group and an EMR Celeborn access security group) so that the entire environment is self-contained, then provisions managed node groups for EMR on EKS Spark workloads: a general node group for system pods with m5.xlarge instances, min/desired size of 2 and max of 3, and a Spark node group for executor pods with memory-optimized r5.2xlarge instances, min/desired size of 3 and max of 6, both on-demand using Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64 standard AMI with 50 GB disk and attaching a launch template that references the newly created security groups, along with an IAM role for the node groups containing the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policies, and a separate IAM role for the EBS CSI driver with the AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy to be used later for IRSA (without deploying the addon), with all instance types, scaling sizes, and a project name parameter defaulting to "emr-celeborn-demo" parameterized, and exporting the two node group names and the CSI driver role name as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained SLO monitoring dashboard and associated CloudWatch alarms for an event-driven pipeline pattern based on FSx for ONTAP, with the following objectives: the template must define four SLO alarms—EventIngestionLatency (P99 threshold of 5 seconds), ProcessingSuccessRate (average threshold of 99.5%), FPolicyReconnectTime (maximum threshold of 30 seconds), and ReplayCompletionTime (maximum threshold of 5 minutes)—each evaluated over three consecutive 5-minute periods with missing data treated as not breaching, and all alarms should optionally forward to an SNS topic if an ARN is provided, but the template must create all other resources itself without relying on pre-existing components. Additionally, the template must create a CloudWatch dashboard that includes time-series metric widgets for each of those four SLO metrics with visual annotations at their thresholds, along with synthetic canary monitoring widgets for S3AP latency (list and get latencies) and ONTAP health check from a separate canary metric namespace, and an alarm status widget listing all four SLO alarms. The entire dashboard and alarm set should only be deployed when an explicit enable flag is set to true (defaulting to false), using a project prefix defaulting to "fsxn-s3ap", a metric namespace defaulting to "FSxN-S3AP-Patterns", and a canary metric namespace defaulting to "FSxN-S3AP-Patterns/Canary", while the region should default to us-east-1 and all thresholds must be configurable via parameters.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates monthly COST budgets for our key security and monitoring services, including AWS Config, CloudWatch, GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, and S3 for security logs, with budget limits of $10,000 for Config and CloudWatch and $1,000 for the remaining services; each budget must be of type COST with a MONTHLY time unit, a defined time period that starts in the past and extends to a distant end date, and the required cost type settings that include recurring, subscription, other-subscription, and upfront charges while excluding credits, discounts, refunds, support, and tax, and the budgets must be retained even if the stack is deleted.

We need a CloudFormation template that deploys a containerized service on AWS Fargate in private subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer. The template should accept the VPC, subnets, ECS cluster, ALB listener, security group, and task execution role as parameters, and create service-specific resources including a CloudWatch log group, task definition with awsvpc networking, target group, ECS service with configurable desired count, and listener rules for traffic routing, with parameters for environment name, service name, Docker image URL, container port, CPU, memory, path pattern, priority, and optional task role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of self-contained Step Functions state machines for testing cross-workflow orchestration, including an EXPRESS state machine that simply succeeds, a STANDARD state machine that uses a synchronous start execution task to invoke the first state machine with definition substitutions, and two additional STANDARD state machines that are also simple succeed states but share a common IAM role; the template must also create the necessary IAM roles with trust policies for Step Functions and attach managed policies that grant the trigger state machine's role permissions to start, stop, and describe executions of the destination state machine, as well as manage EventBridge rules, while the destination state machine's role should have a basic Lambda invocation policy, and all resources should be tagged with a stateMachine:createdBy tag set to SAM.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS service with service discovery and CPU-based autoscaling, importing the ECS cluster name, private service discovery namespace ID, and autoscaling IAM role ARN from another stack via cross-stack references, using configurable parameters for environment name (default 'production'), service name (default 'nginx'), Docker image URL (default 'nginx'), container port (default 80), CPU and memory units (default 256 and 512), desired count (default 2), and an optional IAM role ARN for the task's containers; the template must create a CloudWatch Logs log group, an ECS task definition, a private service discovery service with an SRV DNS record (TTL of 10 seconds) and a custom health check with a failure threshold of 1, an ECS service registered in that discovery service with a deployment configuration of 200% maximum and 75% minimum healthy percent, and an Application Auto Scaling scalable target with a minimum capacity of 2 and maximum capacity of 10, then set up step scaling policies with a 60-second cooldown—a scale-down step that reduces desired count by one when average CPU utilization drops to 20% or below, and a scale-up policy that increases desired count by one, two, or three depending on how much CPU exceeds 70%—both triggered by CloudWatch alarms that evaluate average CPU usage every 60 seconds.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS Fault Injection Simulator experiment template for chaos engineering across multiple regions, designed to disrupt cross-region network connectivity by targeting transit gateways and subnets, and to pause replication for S3 buckets and DynamoDB global tables, all targeting resources tagged with ChaosAllowed set to true, with a configurable experiment duration defaulting to 20 minutes and a target region defaulting to us-east-1, and including a CloudWatch log group encrypted with a new KMS key for experiment logs with a retention period of 7 days, with the experiment template configured to have stop conditions set to none and empty target resolution mode set to skip, all within a single stack that provisions a new IAM role with multiple managed policies attached to allow the FIS service to perform the disruptions.

We need a CloudFormation template that deploys a Docker-based worker service for a voting application to AWS Fargate. The template accepts parameters for all required external infrastructure: the target ECS cluster name, an ECS task execution role ARN, a Fargate security group ID, two public subnet IDs, an Application Auto Scaling role ARN, and a Redis host endpoint. The service also accepts optional parameters for a MongoDB URI and a custom IAM role. Configure the Fargate task definition with 1024 CPU units and 2048 MB of memory, running 2 initial copies, with environment variables for MongoDB URI and Redis host. Enable Application Auto Scaling with step scaling policies triggered by CPU utilization alarms: a scale-down alarm at 20% or lower CPU utilization that removes 1 task, and a scale-up alarm at 70% or higher CPU utilization with step adjustments adding 1 task for a 0-15% threshold breach, 2 tasks for a 15-25% breach, and 3 tasks for a breach above 25%, with a maximum of 10 tasks. Route container logs to a CloudWatch log group named using a combination of the environment name and service name.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a security monitoring system for detecting malicious activity in an AWS account by analyzing CloudTrail logs. The template must accept a configurable stack prefix parameter (defaulting to 'sera'), an optional email parameter for alert notifications, and parameters for the CloudTrail log group name and KMS key ID to use for encryption. Create an SNS topic for security alerts encrypted with the provided KMS key, along with a topic policy allowing CloudWatch to publish to it, and optionally subscribe the provided email address to that topic. Create CloudWatch metric filters on the provided CloudTrail log group that trigger on specific events including: CloudTrail deletion or logging stoppage (critical severity), IAM role policy modifications and IAM user or access key creation (high severity), security group rule additions (medium severity with a threshold of 5 events), VPC network changes like route creation or internet gateway attachment (high severity), and root account usage (critical severity). All alarms must publish to the SNS topic and be configured to treat missing data as not breaching. Export the SNS topic ARN and name for cross-stack reference.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS network backbone designed for hybrid interconnect demonstrations with an OCI primary region, including a VPC, an internet gateway, a private subnet in the first available availability zone, a route table with a default route via the IGW, a transit gateway with a VPC attachment, and a security group that only allows HTTPS inbound from a configurable internal CIDR range and only allows HTTPS outbound to the OCI backbone CIDR; it should also conditionally create a customer gateway and VPN connection to OCI using static routes only, and define a transit gateway route for OCI traffic, all while enabling VPC flow logs encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key that has key rotation enabled and logs stored in CloudWatch with a 30-day retention, and ensuring that all resources use parameterized CIDRs with defaults of 10.94.0.0/16 for the VPC and 10.94.10.0/24 for the subnet.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained infrastructure for a QuickSight admin console data preparation pipeline, including an S3 bucket with a name incorporating the AWS account ID, an IAM role with permissions to assume roles for Glue and CloudFormation and full access to IAM, QuickSight, Glue, S3, CloudWatch, and Logs, and five AWS Glue jobs written in Python (some using PythonShell with version 3.9 and Glue version 3.0, and two using Glue ETL with Glue version 5.0 and G.1X workers) that load scripts from a predefined S3 location; each job is triggered by a separate scheduled Glue trigger set to run every 3 hours, and the stack must output the S3 paths for group membership, object access, folder assets, folder lookup, folder path, and the cloudtrail log table name and S3 location for downstream use.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained disaster recovery failover automation stack for a multi-region application. The stack must provision an IAM execution role and a Lambda function (Python 3.13) that toggles routing control states for a primary region (defaulting to us-east-1) and a secondary standby region. The Lambda function should use the public AWS Lambda Powertools layer, enable active tracing, and dynamically resolve Route53 ARC routing control ARNs and cluster endpoints from Secrets Manager using environment variables. Additionally, the template must provision the necessary IAM service role for Systems Manager and create eight SSM automation documents: four documents to enable/disable the application in the primary and standby regions (by invoking the Lambda function), and four composite failover documents that execute the disable runbook before performing an Aurora global database failover via the RDS FailoverGlobalCluster API (with AllowDataLoss set to true). The SSM documents must reference the global cluster identifiers dynamically from Secrets Manager.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a new VPC, an ECS cluster, an Application Load Balancer with a security group and an HTTP listener on port 80, a Route 53 hosted zone for dliu.com, and all other resources necessary to deploy the "deweiliu/best-friends" container image as an ECS service using EC2 launch type and bridge network mode, with a desired count of 2 tasks that each reserve 256 MB memory and expose container port 8000 mapped to host port 6000, the service should have a health check grace period of 60 seconds, deployment configuration with maximum percent 200 and minimum healthy percent 50, scheduling strategy REPLICA, and ECS managed tags disabled, the service must be associated with a target group of type instance that uses HTTP on port 80 with health checks enabled, and a listener rule on the ALB with priority 60 that forwards traffic based on the host header bfa.dliu.com to that target group, the template must also provision an SSL certificate in ACM for bfa.dliu.com validated via DNS within the hosted zone, attach that certificate to the ALB listener, create a Route 53 CNAME record with TTL 3600 pointing bfa.dliu.com to the load balancer's DNS name, the task definition must have the family name BestFriendsTaskDefinitionFA22AF8E, a placement constraint requiring x86_64 architecture, the container marked as essential, the log driver set to awslogs with stream prefix best-friends and a CloudWatch log group created with default retention, along with an IAM execution role that has permissions to create log streams and put log events, and a separate IAM task role, and the security group on the ECS cluster must allow inbound TCP traffic on port 6000 from the ALB's security group.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates three private subnets (10.24.24.0/24, 10.24.25.0/24, and 10.24.26.0/24) in us-east-1a, us-east-1b, and us-east-1c respectively. Each subnet requires its own route table with a default route pointing to a NAT gateway (provided via three specific NAT gateway parameters, one for each AZ), and each subnet must be associated with a provided network ACL parameter. The template must be fully self-contained, accepting the target VPC ID, the three NAT Gateway IDs, and the Network ACL ID as standard parameters instead of relying on cross-stack imports. Additionally, provision an S3 VPC endpoint attached to all three route tables with a full-access policy. Finally, export a comma-separated list of the private subnet IDs, the route table IDs, and the subnet group CIDR (10.24.24.0/21) using export names constructed dynamically from the region and stack name. Tag all resources using the stack name and meaningful resource names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a complete EC2 Image Builder pipeline for building and managing custom AMIs, including a custom component that downloads and executes a Chef recipe from an S3 bucket, an image recipe using the latest Amazon Linux 2 ECS optimized AMI as the parent image with a root volume of appropriate size and type, an infrastructure configuration that terminates instances on failure, a distribution configuration that shares the resulting AMI with the current account in a target region, an image pipeline scheduled to run daily with image scanning and tests enabled, a lifecycle policy that deprecates AMIs based on age and tag selection, and a custom build workflow that updates the SSM agent and collects metadata before creating the AMI; all required IAM roles and instance profiles must be created as part of the stack, and the template should use parameters for any configurable names or regions with sensible defaults.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates three private subnets (10.24.32.0/24, 10.24.33.0/24, and 10.24.34.0/24) in us-east-1a, us-east-1b, and us-east-1c respectively. Each subnet requires its own route table with a default route pointing to a NAT gateway (provided via three specific NAT gateway parameters, one for each AZ), and each subnet must be associated with a provided network ACL parameter. The template must be fully self-contained and assume the VPC already exists, accepting the target VPC ID as a parameter. Create an S3 VPC Gateway Endpoint attached to all three route tables. Create a security group allowing inbound HTTPS traffic from the VPC CIDR (10.24.0.0/16). Provision one OpenSearch Serverless VPC endpoint and four Interface VPC endpoints for Bedrock services (bedrock, bedrock-agent, bedrock-runtime, and bedrock-agent-runtime). All interface endpoints must be placed in the first and third private subnets, use the created security group, have private DNS enabled, and include a resource policy allowing access from the current account and a specified external account parameter. Export a comma-separated list of the private subnet IDs, the route table IDs, the subnet group CIDR (10.24.32.0/21), and each VPC endpoint ID, utilizing the region and stack name in the export names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM execution role for a SageMaker HyperPod cluster integrated with an EKS cluster, where the template accepts parameters for a resource name prefix, an EKS cluster name, a VPC ID, a list of security group IDs, a list of private subnet IDs, an S3 bucket name for lifecycle scripts, and optional parameters for a RIG input S3 bucket, a RIG output S3 bucket, a flag to create RIG resources, and a flag to enable gated access, and the role must be named by appending "ExecRole" to the prefix, allow the SageMaker service principal to assume it, be attached to the AWS managed policy for SageMaker cluster instance roles, and include a custom inline policy that grants the EKS CNI plugin permissions for attaching network interfaces, describing instances, tags, network interfaces, instance types, and subnets, and creating tags on network interfaces, along with a second inline policy that grants broader ENI management actions such as assigning private IP addresses, creating, deleting, and modifying network interfaces and permissions, and detaching network interfaces, scoped to instances, network interfaces, and the specified VPC, Provision a public subnet and a private subnet in each of the three availability zones, an Internet Gateway for public routing, NAT Gateways with Elastic IPs in each public subnet to enable private subnet outbound internet access, public and private route tables with appropriate associations, Network Access Control Lists for both public and private subnets, and an S3 VPC endpoint for private resource access to S3 services without internet transit.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates foundational account-level IAM infrastructure for Amazon EKS Quick Start deployments. The template should create multiple Lambda execution roles with appropriate policies: a CopyZips role for reading deployment artifacts from S3, a ResourceReader role with read-only access to all AWS resources, a CreateVpcRole for VPC creation and IAM role attachment operations, a DeleteBucketContents role, and roles for managing Lambda lifecycle, cleaning up load balancers and security groups, resolving CloudFormation stack parameters, and registering EKS custom resource types. Include an EKS cluster control plane role with the AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSServicePolicy managed policies, along with permissions to describe EC2 resources and internet gateways. Create EC2 instance profiles and corresponding IAM roles for both managed and unmanaged EKS worker nodes, granting permissions for EKS worker node operations, CNI plugin functionality, ECR read-only access, and EFS read-only access. Define Fargate pod execution roles with assume-role trust policy for eks-fargate-pods.amazonaws.com and the AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy managed policy. Include a ParameterResolver role with permissions to read parameters from SSM Parameter Store under the /quickstart/amazon-eks path. All IAM roles should follow a standardized naming convention using the prefix 'eks-quickstart' with role-specific suffixes, and the template should use CloudFormation mappings for configurable naming. The template should not provision any compute, networking, or storage resources, focusing exclusively on IAM role and permission setup.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a multi-tier VPC architecture with a CIDR block of 10.128.0.0/16 spanning three availability zones for high availability, featuring a public web tier, a private application tier, and a private database tier. The web tier should contain public subnets with CIDR blocks 10.128.0.0/24, 10.128.1.0/24, and 10.128.2.0/24 attached to an Internet Gateway for inbound and outbound internet access, sharing one route table across all three availability zones. The application tier should contain private subnets with CIDR blocks 10.128.10.0/24, 10.128.11.0/24, and 10.128.12.0/24, each with its own route table directing outbound internet traffic through a NAT Gateway in the corresponding web-tier availability zone. The database tier should contain private subnets with CIDR blocks 10.128.20.0/24, 10.128.21.0/24, and 10.128.22.0/24, each with its own route table similarly routing through NAT Gateways, and each NAT Gateway should be allocated an Elastic IP address. The template should output the VPC ID, subnet lists for each tier, the CIDR block, and the availability zones.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with native IPv6 support and flexible public and private subnet configuration. The template should accept configurable parameters for the VPC identifier name and CIDR block, with an option to include or exclude public subnets. If public subnets are enabled, provision an Internet Gateway and configure a public route table to direct internet-bound traffic through it. Automatically divide the VPC CIDR block into nine equal subnets distributed across the available availability zones, allocating the first three as public subnets (if enabled) and the remaining six as private subnets. Each subnet should receive both an IPv4 allocation and an IPv6 allocation derived from the VPC's IPv6 CIDR block, with instances configured to automatically receive IPv6 addresses. Apply appropriate tags to distinguish public from private subnets and resources.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the complete IAM infrastructure for Kubernetes Cluster API Provider on AWS with EKS support. The template should provision three instance profiles tied to IAM roles for control plane nodes, worker nodes, and Kubernetes API controllers, along with a separate EKS control plane service role. Attach managed policies to these roles that grant permissions for Kubernetes cloud provider operations including EC2 instance lifecycle management, security group and network interface operations, VPC creation and management, load balancing configuration, and auto-scaling group integration. Include policies that enable controllers to manage VPC resources, transit gateway attachments, launch templates, and IAM service-linked roles. Add EKS-specific policies for cluster, node group, addon, and access entry management. Provide a managed policy for EKS console users to view clusters, node groups, and access the Kubernetes API. All policies should enforce appropriate resource constraints and use conditions to follow the principle of least privilege.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained Student Services agent infrastructure for an educational platform using AWS Bedrock AgentCore, where each agent or microservice domain gets its own Cognito user pool for OAuth2 client credentials authentication and its own IAM execution role with least-privilege permissions specific to its function. The template should include a shared base IAM managed policy granting Bedrock model invocation, CloudWatch logging and metrics under the bedrock-agentcore namespace, X-Ray tracing, and Systems Manager parameter access for the student-services path, and attach this base policy to every execution role. For the StudentServicesAgent orchestrator, create only the execution role without a Cognito pool because its inbound authentication is IAM-based. For the StudentServicesGateway, create a Cognito user pool, a custom domain using the account ID, a resource server with an access scope, and a confidential app client using client_credentials flow, but no execution role. For the CourseRegistration domain, create an execution role that includes the base policy plus full DynamoDB access, along with self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the CourseCatalog domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus an inline policy allowing bedrock:Retrieve on any knowledge base, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the CourseReview domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus DynamoDB read-only access, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the LoanApplication domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus an inline policy allowing sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint on any SageMaker endpoint, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. All Cognito user pools should have relaxed password policies, auto-verify email, and require email as a schema attribute. All execution roles should assume trust by the bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com service with source account and source ARN conditions. The stack should export each execution role ARN, each user pool ID, each OIDC discovery URL, each app client ID, each token endpoint constructed from the custom domain pattern, and each OAuth scope for downstream cross-stack consumption.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained bootstrap environment for deploying AWS CDK applications, including an encrypted S3 bucket for file assets with versioning and HTTPS-only access, an immutable ECR repository with image scanning for container assets, a KMS key for bucket encryption with a customizable alias, IAM roles for file publishing, image publishing, account lookup, deployment actions, and CloudFormation execution with configurable trusted accounts and managed policy ARNs, an SSM parameter to track the bootstrap version, and support for custom asset bucket names or using an existing KMS key, all using a short qualifier string to uniquely identify the stack components in the same AWS account and region.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS AppSync GraphQL API named "TodoAPIwithJs" with API key authentication, backed by a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index on the owner attribute, and using JavaScript resolvers to support full CRUD operations (create, update, delete, get, list) as well as a query by owner index, along with real-time subscriptions for create, update, and delete events, all implemented as pipeline resolvers with individual JavaScript functions for each data operation.
